segments.text: A humpback whale shuts its mouth around a lobster diver. About thirty seconds later, it spits him out. Alive.
No chance. Whales don't eat people. Let's go look.
June {2021|twenty twenty-one}. Off Cape Cod, Michael Packard is {45|forty-five} feet down, hunting for lobsters.
Something hits him like a truck. The world goes black. He thinks: shark. But there are no teeth.
He's in a whale's mouth, still breathing from his tank. He thinks of his wife and his sons.
Then the whale surfaces, shakes its head, and throws him out. His crewmate gets him aboard.
Bruised, but no broken bones. He's home by the afternoon.
Scientists call it an accident. The whale was feeding, and its throat is too narrow to swallow a man. So I was right. And wrong. Case closed.
